subject: Tranche commit triggers & regional sizing for HelixCorp
messages:
From: aisha.rahman@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: sam.ortega@helixcorp.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Helix request: tranche-level commit triggers for regional pools

Team —

HelixCorp ops (Sam) asked for a simple matrix that ties deal tranches (commit $ / committed qps) to actual dedicated capacity we would reserve in US / EU / APAC. They want clarity on:
- what minimum committed QPS or token throughput unlocks a dedicated mini-pool in each region,
- how we handle burst vs sustained (i.e., burst credits, buffer GPU weeks),
- what latency SLOs are guaranteed per tranche and where the fallback model kicks in.

Attached is the Excel template they shared (helix_tranche_template.xlsx). Please populate rough numbers for GPU types we typically provision (A10G / H100-equivalent), and a fallback policy for preemptive routing to hosted variants.

Can someone take the initial pass? Markus asked we keep it conservative — they have multiple product teams and want predictable cost math for procurement.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

(attachment: helix_tranche_template.xlsx)
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Date: 2027-04-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helix request: tranche-level commit triggers for regional pools

Thanks Aisha — taking this on. A few clarifying items before we fill numbers:

1) Is Helix asking for strictly reserved (dedicated) GPUs or a hybrid (dedicated + burst to hosted) approach for each tranche? They mentioned procurement prefers reserved capacity where predictable but will accept burst in APAC for first 6 months.
2) Do they want the matrix in weekly-GPU-weeks or vCPU-equivalent? I’d prefer GPU-weeks — easier to map to Dedicated SKU pricing.
3) Level of SLA: For larger tranches (> $250k / mo commit) should we guarantee 99th percentile token latency < 250ms in US/EU and < 350ms in APAC (given cross-region egress)?

I sketched a starter matrix (inline) — still rough. I attached a PDF summary (regional-sizing-draft.pdf) and exported a CSV (lauren_commit_matrix_v1.csv).

Starter (example rows):
- Tranche A: commit >= $50k/mo -> US: 4 GPU-weeks sustained (A10G equiv), EU: 2 GPU-weeks, APAC: 1 GPU-week (burst eligible)
- Tranche B: commit >= $150k/mo -> US: 12 GPU-weeks (H100 equiv), EU: 6 GPU-weeks, APAC: 4 GPU-weeks (burst buffer 20%)
- Tranche C: commit >= $350k/mo -> US: 30 GPU-weeks (H100), EU: 18 GPU-weeks, APAC: 12 GPU-weeks; 99th p50 targets tightened, dedicated-only

Open items for engineering: mapping commit $ to expected sustained token throughput and identifying whether multi-model mixing increases required headroom. Karthik / Rishi — can you weight the headroom assumptions (sustained vs burst) and confirm the GPU type mapping by region?

Next step: finalize matrix, get Helix procurement to sign off on tranche definitions, then we draft SOW language for Dedicated pools.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

(attachment: regional-sizing-draft.pdf)
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, aisha.rahman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sam.ortega@helixcorp.com
Date: 2027-04-24T14:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helix request: tranche-level commit triggers for regional pools

Adding technical constraints and suggested conservative headroom calculations.

Summary notes:
- GPU flavors: map H100-equivalent to "high-throughput" tranche (Tranche B/C). Use A10G-equivalent for lower tranches and APAC burst lanes. Physical provisioning in APAC is slower; treat first 8 weeks as warm-up (canary) with burst to hosted.
- Headroom math: assume 35% overhead for KV cache variability and 25% for mixed-model interference. That means for a target sustained QPS we multiply by 1.6 to get GPU-weeks required.
- Burst policy: allow 30% short-term burst credit for <= 10 minutes per minute-window, reconciled monthly. If monthly burst > 15% of sustained, trigger automatic increase to next tranche.
- Fallback: if regional Dedicated pool saturated, requests route to nearest region's Dedicated pool (cost-adjusted) and then to hosted API as last resort. Document the expected 95% latency impact when cross-region fallback occurs.

Practical example (back-of-envelope): Helix wants 200 rps sustained in US for a generative chat workload with 60-token average output -> approx 12k tokens/sec -> roughly maps to 8 H100-weeks sustained after headroom. That aligns with Tranche B when combined with EU/APAC demand.

I attached a short calc sheet in the Drive link and flagged ops safety items.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal, Serving Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Procurement leans toward reserved capacity for Tranche B and above; Tranche A they expect a hybrid model for the first 3 months.
2) Can you add explicit canary language? We want a 30-day canary with success metrics (latency and error rate) before full activation of a Dedicated pool in a region.
3) For legal: we need a clear fallback SLA clause that defines customer-visible behavior when routing crosses regions (e.g., we must notify Helix within 10 minutes and provide mitigation steps).

If you can send a redline-friendly SOW paragraph and a commit-trigger table, procurement will try to include it in the vendor evaluation this week.

Sam Ortega
Head of Platform Engineering, HelixCorp

Subject: Re: Helix request: tranche-level commit triggers for regional pools — proposal & next steps

Sam / team —

Thanks for the quick feedback. Attached are final artifacts for procurement: lauren_commit_matrix_v1.csv (commit trigger matrix), a 2-paragraph SOW snippet below (redline-friendly), and a short canary checklist. Quick summary of decisions we propose:

- Tranche definitions (final):
  * Tranche A (Entry): commit $50k–$149k/mo — hybrid: Dedicated reserved in US only (A10G equiv), EU/APAC via burst to hosted for first 90 days. Canary period: 30 days.
  * Tranche B (Growth): commit $150k–$349k/mo — Dedicated reserved in US + EU (H100 equiv), APAC dedicated as optional 60-day ramp with burst credit. 99th percentile latency targets: US/EU < 250ms, APAC < 350ms.
  * Tranche C (Enterprise): >= $350k/mo — Dedicated reserved in US/EU/APAC (H100 equiv), 99th p token latency < 200ms US/EU. Dedicated-only; burst offload disabled except emergency fallback.

- Canary policy: 30-day canary with success criteria: error rate < 0.5%, P95 latency within 1.25x of production target, and sustained utilization < 70% for two nonconsecutive weeks. If canary fails, we either increase buffer capacity or extend the canary by 14 days.

- Fallback & notification: if autoscaling cannot satisfy burst and we route cross-region or to hosted, Redwood will: (1) notify Helix via Ops Pager within 10 minutes, (2) open a joint incident channel, and (3) provide a remediation timeline and cost impact within 4 hours. This phrasing is in the SOW snippet we attached for legal to redline.

Next actions:
- Aisha: share lauren_commit_matrix_v1.csv with Helix procurement (completed).
- Marissa: prepare SOW paragraph for legal redlines and include DocuSign link -> I added HubSpot link below.
- Karthik & Rishi: finalize the GPU-weeks to throughput mapping in the Drive sheet and mark any region-specific provisioning lead times.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HLX-2027-0428
Drive: https://redwood-sharing/drive/helix-sizing-draft

If there are no objections, we'll aim to have a redline-ready packet to Helix by EOD Friday and target procurement signoff next week.
